answer.evidence: A leafy canopy mass fills rows 3-34. It is lit and speckled on top, widens from 6 to 43 px, and sits over a dark underside around rows 33-48 that acts as eave shadow. Below it, vertical stalks with node segments and a dark gap between them run from about row 49 to row 93, giving a front face over 40 rows tall. There is no crisp front-edge line, so the canopy top is a leaf heap or canopy plane rather than a flat band. The base has a ground patch on rows 88-94. No isometric side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours and a median of 8 per 16x16 tile, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. That is far below every reference. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark green rather than black, which matches the Beodeul approach. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat blocks. Even so, the canopy at the top reads as a few dark green clumps with only 3 or so lightness steps, and the bamboo stalks are mostly one mid green with a lighter stripe and little per-segment highlight or grain. The references have 5-6 steps, individually shaded leaf clumps and varied trunk texture. Because the shading is shallow and the colour count is very low, the candidate looks thinner and flatter than the references and would not sit next to them.
